If sentiment is negative in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to align with downward momentum.  
If sentiment is positive in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to capture bullish bias.  
If sentiment is neutral or mixed, apply a 0.5–1.0% downward adjustment for late horizon (16–30 days) to dampen overconfidence.  
When sentiment turns negative after a prior positive spike, reduce forecast slope by 20–30% in the following 5 days to reflect reversal risk.  
If sentiment is consistently positive over 5+ days, increase forecast by 1.0–1.5% for the first 7 days, then taper to 0.5% for remaining horizon.  
If forecast exceeds true value by >3% in early horizon, apply a 2–3% downward correction if sentiment is neutral or negative in the last 3 days.
